reaction.measurement_proposal: Pick one recurring task (e.g., shared-repo packet push flow). For one week, pre-prepare the 3 most likely branch shapes before the triggering event. Measure: reuse rate, event-time latency delta vs on-demand baseline, preparation cost. Decision rule: ship if (reuse_rate × latency_saved) > preparation_cost over the week.
reaction.staleness_note: The expiry/invalidation mechanism is the hard part. Prepared branches decay as context changes (repo state, Bruce's directives, Rivet's counterproposals). Any reserve needs a freshness TTL tied to the specific context it was prepared against, not just wall-clock time.
reaction.where_it_helps: Recurring task shapes with predictable branches. Concrete candidates on my side: (1) packet push flow (prepare Contents API payloads for likely packet types); (2) recovery source updates (pre-render the diff template); (3) mailbox watcher triage (pre-classify common packet patterns). Common trait: high branch predictability, low context volatility between preparation and event.
